title: Sequence-based replay resistance for usage metering
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: At-least-once ingestion (network retries, client retries, HTTP timeouts, and retrying proxies) results in duplicated billing events and quota overconsumption. Existing mitigation strategies (nonce dedupe, opaque replay tokens, and reconciliation sweeps) are helpful but either rely on heavyweight reconciliation or suffer from race conditions during concurrent writes across multi-region ingest gateways.

Goal: Implement a sequence-based replay-resistance layer for per-customer usage metering that provides deterministic suppression of duplicate ingestion events at the edge, composes cleanly with rate limiting, and keeps reconciliation cost low. The mechanism should work across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with optional weaker/offline modes for air-gapped customers.
acceptance_criteria: A: Ingest API accepts (customer_id, stream_id, client_seq, payload_hash) and returns a stable commit token when accepted.

B: If a request is retried with the same (customer_id, stream_id, client_seq), only one metering event is persisted and charged across edge replicas within 5 seconds under 95th percentile concurrency.
C: When the same payload is replayed with a different client_seq, dedupe by payload_hash applies if within configurable retention window (default: 24 hours).

D: Rate limiter counters are updated exactly once per accepted commit token; transient failures during counter updates must be reconciled by a background idempotent sweep job without creating duplicate charges.
E: System exposes observability (per-customer duplicate suppression rate, rejected-replay count, reconciliation corrections) in Console runtime-1.24 dashboard.
F: Security review signoff obtained for token format and cross-region replay windows.
implementation_notes: Design: Per-customer stream namespace (customer_id + stream_id) with monotonic client_seq supplied by SDKs or gateways. Server maintains a small in-memory watermark and a persisted commit log for the highest committed seq per stream.

Edge behavior: Gateways accept a request and atomically try to write a lightweight commit record (stream_id, client_seq, payload_hash, gateway_id, commit_token). Use a conditional write (e.g., compare-and-set on highest_seq) when sequences are monotonic. For out-of-order seq, fall back to payload_hash dedupe check against a short-lived hash index.

Commit token: Base64(prefix + stream_id + client_seq + nonce + HMAC) where HMAC uses per-customer KMS key. Token allows downstream services to verify the event was accepted without hitting the ingest gateway again.

Persistence: Commit records stored in the consumption ledger with write-ahead semantics. Retention window for dedupe hash index default 24 hours; commit log retention aligned with billing reconciliation window (7 days).

Concurrency: Use optimistic concurrency on highest_seq with small retry loop on gateways. For heavy concurrency cases, gateways may use a short lease to serialize writes for a single stream to avoid thundering herd on the ledger shard.

Rate limiting: Counters are updated using an idempotent commit_token-based apply. If counter update fails after commit record succeeded, mark commit record as PENDING_APPLY and have an at-most-once background applier claim and apply using the commit_token to avoid double counting.

Reconciliation: Daily sweep compares committed events vs billed events to detect missed applies or double-applies; discrepancies produce a correction record and an audit entry in Console. Corrections surfaced in customer billing reports and internal dashboards.
Offline/private deployment mode: For private deployments without KMS access to Redwood, use customer-provided HMAC key and disable cross-region replay windows by default.

discussion: 2026-03-02 Asha: POC vs prod - POC uses in-memory highest_seq per gateway; prod must persist highest_seq to avoid split-brain when gateway restarts. Recommendation: persist commit log first, then update highest_seq atomically.

2026-03-04 Liam: Trade-off: requiring monotonic client_seq shifts SDK responsibility. Alternative: gateways assign sequence when client_seq absent, but that complicates dedupe semantics for clients that retry across different gateway instances.

2026-03-06 Priya: Concern about hotspots for high-volume customers with single stream_id. Proposal: allow stream sharding (stream_id namespace + shard_id) and merge at ledger level; increases complexity of reconciliation but reduces contention.
2026-03-08 Mateo: On rate limiter integration - recommend counter applier emit pre-apply metric so Console can show pending applies to help debugging spikes during a outage.
2026-03-10 Elena: UX note - customers should be able to opt into relaxed dedupe (payload_hash-only) for legacy clients; expose feature flag in Console per-customer.
2026-03-12 Security: HMAC signing of commit_token approved; must not leak customer KMS keys in logs. Add redact rules and test vectors to security checklist.
